title: Ezogelin Soup
subtitle: Turkish red lentil and bulgur soup with buttered paprika
excerpt: A thick, warming Turkish soup of red lentils and bulgur, finished with a swirl of paprika butter. It is simple to make and ready in under 40 minutes. The butter finish goes on at the very end and makes a real difference.
sourceNotes: Named after Ezo Gelin, a bride from Gaziantep. Now served across Turkey as a starter or light meal, especially at breakfast in the south-east.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the paprika butter. Reheat on the hob, add water to loosen if needed, then make the butter finish fresh.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales easily. Use a large saucepan and keep the heat low so the lentils do not catch.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the soup up to 3 days ahead and keep chilled. Reheat gently and make the butter finish just before serving.

content.text: Ezogelin is a thick Turkish lentil and bulgur soup. It comes together quickly and the main work is in the finish: a sizzle of butter and paprika poured over at the last moment. Do not skip this step; it transforms the soup from plain to distinctly Turkish.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree, sweet paprika, cumin, and dried mint. Cook for 2 minutes until the paste smells fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils and pour in the stock. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20 minutes. Stir occasionally so the lentils do not stick to the base.
Add the bulgur wheat and cook for a further 10 minutes until the bulgur is soft and the soup is thick. Blend until smooth with a stick blender. Season with salt.
Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the hot paprika and swirl for 30 seconds until the butter turns deep red and fragrant.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Drizzle the hot paprika butter over each bowl and serve straight away.

items.cause: The lentils absorbed more liquid than expected.
items.fix: Add boiling water or stock a little at a time until you reach the consistency you want. Stir well and taste for seasoning.

items.symptom: The soup sticks to the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: The heat was too high once the bulgur went in.
items.fix: Keep the heat on the lowest setting after adding the bulgur and stir every 2 minutes.

items.cause: The butter got too hot and the paprika scorched.
items.fix: Heat the butter until it just foams, then take the pan off the heat before adding the paprika. The residual heat is enough.
